content.title: How Real Madrid eliminated 10-man Manchester City from Champions League after Vinicius Jr second-leg double
content.text: Real Madrid are on course to face Bayern Munich in the quarter-final after a 5-1 aggregate winGeorge Ramsay and Ed MackeyMarch 17, 2026 at 6:10 PM CDTVinicius Jr scored both Real Madrid goals as they won 2-1 in Manchester. Getty ImagesReal Madrid eliminate Manchester City, advance to quarter-finalsReal Madrid have eliminated Manchester City from the Champions League after winning 5-1 over two legs.Pep Guardiola’s men were facing an uphill task after a 3-0 defeat in the first leg and that was made almost impossible when Bernardo Silva was sent off for handball in the 20th minute.Vinicius Jr, who had a penalty saved in the first leg, sent Gianluigi Donnarumma the wrong way to make it 4-0 on aggregate. Erling Haaland reduced the arrears before half-time but he and his team-mates were unable to make further inroads into the deficit.Vinicius Jr scored deep in stoppage time — after seeing a goal disallowed moments before — to give Madrid a 2-1 win on the night,Real Madrid and Bayern Munich look set to meet in the quarter-final.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWhat's next for both teams? Getty ImagesThere are two big games coming up for both teams this weekend. Manchester City face Arsenal in the EFL Cup final at Wembley on Sunday — a great chance to put their disappointing Champions League exit behind them by lifting some silverware. Real Madrid, meanwhile, face local rivals Atletico at the Bernabeu on the same day, pitting second against third in La Liga. At this point in the season, the big games seem to come thick and fast. Four more matches on the way tomorrow! Getty ImagesSo, one night of last-16 second legs down and one more to come tomorrow. And there is plenty still to play for in those matches.It feels unlikely that Atalanta and Tottenham will progress but the other two ties are very much still up in the air.5:45pmBarcelona vs Newcastle (1-1 agg.) – covered live on The Athletic8pmBayern Munich vs Atalanta (6-1 agg.)Liverpool vs Galatasaray (0-1 agg.) – covered live on The AthleticTottenham vs Atletico Madrid (2-5 agg.)All times GMTUCL results: Arsenal into the quarters, Chelsea thrashed by PSG Getty ImagesIt was another tough night for two Premier League teams as Manchester City gave themselves too much to do and Chelsea were hammered again by PSG, this time at Stamford Bridge.One English side who booked their quarter-final place were Arsenal, though they were made to work hard for their 2-0 win against Bayer Leverkusen with Eberechi Eze and Declan Rice getting the goals.The early kick-off ended in heartbreak for Bodo/Glimt as they were beaten 5-0 after extra time by Sporting CP.Sporting CP 5-0 (AET) Bodo/Glimt (3-5 agg.)Arsenal 2-0 Bayer Leverkusen (3-1 agg.)Chelsea 0-3 PSG (2-8 agg.)Manchester City 1-2 Real Madrid (1-4 agg.)Guardiola: 'I just want the chance to play 11 against 11' Getty ImagesPep Guardiola was left to wonder what might have been with Bernardo Silva's red card still clearly running through his mind — here is what he said to Prime Video.💬 “Just the feeling of what would have happened (if it was) 11 against 11, that's the feeling. It's difficult 4-0 down with 10 against 11 but we gave everything.“We have an extraordinary team, an extraordinary group of players, the future is bright.“I know how we were going to play. I just want the chance to play 11 against 11, that's all.”Where does this leave Guardiola and City? Getty ImagesCity certainly gave it all that they had, but that may never have been enough — even before Bernardo’s instinctive but extremely costly red card.It has been a difficult week for City and Guardiola after the 3-0 defeat at the Bernabeu and the 1-1 draw at West Ham. Those results made it hard to believe that a comeback was ever on here, but the way that City played both before and after the red card will surely mean they emerge from this tie with credit in the bank.That said, Madrid’s counter-attack was a massive threat both before and after the red card, and Vinicius Jr could have had at least a hat-trick.The way that City stuck at it may not seem like much, but this is a team that is growing. Many people seem to have doubts, but with commitment like this it does suggest their ceiling is very high and that, next season, they can come back much stronger.If Guardiola believes that, too, he may yet see out that final year of his contract.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementHow did Guardiola mix things up? Getty ImagesManchester City’s initial set-up was as attacking as possible, with arguably their most functional frontline, featuring Jeremy Doku, Haaland and Rayan Cherki.While Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush have been in impressive form lately, Guardiola admitted in his press conference after the 1-1 draw with West Ham United that he got it wrong.The trio lined up ahead of their most attack-minded midfielder in Tijjani Reijnders, with Bernardo Silva and Rodri also pushing into attacking areas in the early minutes. That led to chances for Reijnders and Rodri early in the game, only to be denied by a last-ditch Dean Huijsen block and a save from Courtois respectively.Bernardo’s dismissal led to City largely ditching their coordinated high press and falling slightly deeper. Madrid were able to find the spare man to hold onto possession and target runs in behind — like they did in the lead-up to their goal — which reduced City’s threat further in the final 10 minutes before half-time.Bringing on Marc Guehi and Nathan Ake at half-time was not the defensive shift it looked to be on paper. Together with the impressive Khusanov, they formed a back three with the full-backs pushing well ahead and wide, allowing Doku to pop up in central areas closer to Cherki and behind Haaland.City maintained that shape after Guardiola switched Haaland and Matheus Nunes for Marmoush and Semenyo. Unfortunately for the City coach, it was not enough to complete a huge task tonight.Alexander-Arnold: ‘We came here to win’ Getty ImagesLet's hear from Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold after his side reached the Champions League quarter-finals.💬 “There's an expectation when you join the club to go far in this competition and win it. I think everybody knows that the Champions League is embedded in the identity of the club. “There's an expectation and we thrive with that. It brings the best out of us... Over the two legs, we deserved to go through.” And here's what he said about Madrid's approach tonight:“Our mentality was to come here and win. We came in with a three-goal advantage but we didn't want to just sit back and hope that they didn't score and get back into the tie. It was about coming here and winning and we've done that.” Courtois maybe the best goalkeeper in history, says Arbeloa Getty ImagesSpeaking to Prime Video, Alvaro Arbeloa was understandably wearing a beaming smile — here is what he had to say about the result.💬 “So happy. We have beaten Man City at home and everyone knows how difficult that is — we're really with the score. It's not easy to beat Man City 5-1 while we're missing key players against a coach like Pep.The Real Madrid head coach was then asked whether his goalkeeper, Thibaut Courtois, is the best in the world.“I think so, maybe he's the best in history. We are so happy to have him with us.”Vinicius Jr has the last laugh Getty ImagesFor Vinicius Jr, it was another dramatic evening in the Champions League: a performance full of menace and attacking threat, an important goal, a succession of missed chances and the usual howls of derision from a home crowd unnerved by his talent.Manchester City’s supporters thought they had the ammunition to get under his skin, serenading him with “Where’s your Ballon d’Or?” (to the strains of “Chirpy Chirpy Cheep Cheep” by Middle of the Road, if you’re wondering). That was a reference to his and Madrid’s sense of outrage when the winger was beaten to the award by City midfielder Rodri in 2024. There were chants of “cheat, cheat, cheat” after he responded theatrically to a first-half tangle with Khusanov.But Vinicius Jr laughed loudest and last. He only scored once, from the penalty spot after his shot was blocked on the line by Bernardo Silva’s arm, but he was a thorn in City’s side all evening. His speed and the intelligence of his movement caused so many problems. His second goal being ruled offside in the closing stages provoked amusement from the home crowd, who had been riled by his celebration — but even then, he had the final say, completing his double in stoppage time. He didn’t hold back with his celebrations and, frankly, why should he?Doku disappointed with defeat after strong showing Getty ImagesHere's what Man City's Jeremy Doku said to Prime Video after his side's 5-1 aggregate defeat. 💬 “I feel like we had a lot of chances. We played well, especially with 10 against 11, playing against a team like that, it's always going to be difficult. But we did well. Obviously, we're disappointed with the loss today.“It's a hard reality. I feel like when you experience a game, it doesn't feel like they were much better than us. But when you look at the score, it's obvious. That was not the case, that's why it's a bit disappointing for us.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementVinicius Jr explains crying celebration Getty ImagesAs part of his celebration for his first goal, Vinicius Jr gestured that he was crying to the Manchester City fans behind the goal. Speaking to Prime Video after the match, the Brazilian explained it.💬 “The last time I came to Manchester City, they were making fun of me and saying I was crying (about the Ballon d’Or). I wasn’t disrespecting the City fans but it was just a way for me to prove myself to the Manchester City fans.”Answer translated by Prime Video's Alex AljoeMan City fought bravely with 10 men The AthleticBased just of The Athletic's signature match dashboard, you would not know that City were down to 10 men. They had nearly as much possession (48%) and a much higher field tilt (68%) while creating nearly as much xG as Madrid did from open play (2.2).Ultimately, they gave themselves too big of a hole to dig out of by losing the first leg 3-0 and going down to 10 men after a period of early dominance, but there are plenty of positives for them to take. Madrid, despite the convincing margin of their victory overall, will know they have weaknesses to iron out before the quarter-finals, which will likely pit them against a juggernaut in Bayern Munich.Vinicius Jr: ‘We are ready for more’ Getty ImagesHere's what Vinicius Jr had to say to Movistar TV after his brace handed Real Madrid a 2-1 win on the night.💬 “This was a really important tie for our confidence, as from the start of the season we had many good games but we did not have as much control as in this tie. “This was a very difficult game against a great team and great coach. They had the ball a lot but we knew what we had to do, work hard, and take our chances. Although today I missed a lot of chances.”“It is an important moment. All the players, we knew the big games were coming. And when Madrid play in this competition everything changes — the fans change, the players change and we are ready for more, for the next round.”Arbeloa makes history for Real Madrid Getty ImagesAs Dermot says, Real Madrid look a lot more stable under Alvaro Arbeloa, even if they have fallen away slightly from Barcelona in the title race.Thanks to that very late Vinicius Jr goal, the Spaniard becomes the first manager in the club's history to win his first four Champions League matches in charge.It won't count for much if they are beaten by Bayern Munich in the quarter-final, though.Full-time scenes Getty ImagesReal Madrid's dominance in the first leg ultimately laid the foundations for their progress to the quarter-finals, with Man City simply having too much to do this evening, especially after going down to 10 men.The away team are understandably delighted with the result as they celebrate on the Etihad pitch. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCity can take positives despite defeat Getty ImagesIt's funny how football works. The City fans did not seem to be especially hopeful or, dare I say, united ahead of this match, largely thanks to the defeat last week and the draw at West Ham. But even in defeat here the team and players seem to have emerged closer together. A sense of injustice has probably helped that, as well as the antics of arch villain Vinicius Jr, who tried to rile the crowd all night despite his glut of missed chances, but the efforts of the City players have not gone unnoticed. It might be a stretch to say that they go out with their heads held high, given the manner of the defeat last week, but they certainly gave a good account for themselves and I believe that bodes well for their future.Madrid go through to the quarter-finals for the 13th time in the last 15 seasons.In that time, they’ve been to the semis 12 times and won the final six times.Real Madrid revitalised under Arbeloa Getty ImagesThe winner of this tie has often won the Champions League trophy in recent years (Madrid in 2022, City in 2023, Madrid in 2024).There's a long way to go yet, with powerful-looking Bayern probably coming up in the quarter-finals, but the same Madrid squad which was struggling under Xabi Alonso earlier this season looks revitalised under Arbeloa’s less complicated management style.FULL TIME: Real Madrid eliminate Manchester City again Getty ImagesFT Manchester City 1-2 Real Madrid (1-5 agg.)Real Madrid are through and will likely face Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals. Manchester City have failed to reach the last eight for the second year in a row
